notes.decision: ⲡⲓⲇ appears three times (lines 14, 16) flanking the chapter heading. Almost certainly a paragraph/section marker (perhaps abbreviation of παράγραφος or Coptic chapter-marker), not lexical content. Translated as '(¶)'.

Read as ⲛ̄(ⲇⲓ)ⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ 'righteous' (Greek δίκαιος); the form shows scribal variation (loss of -ⲇⲓ-) but the sense is secured by Manichaean usage of ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ as a designation of the Elect (cf. accumulated ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲣⲙ̄ⲙⲏⲉ).

Read as 'the Illuminator' (= Mani). Likely an orthographic variant or scribal form of ⲡⲡⲛ̄ⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ 'our Illuminator' (in glossary) or ⲡⲓ-ⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ 'this Illuminator' with intrusive ⲛ. The ⲡⲓⲛϥ- cluster is unusual but the referent is unambiguous: Mani as φωστήρ addressing his disciples in standard Kephalaia narrative frame.
ⲉⲕⲩⲉⲕⲧⲟⲥ = ἐκλεκτός 'elect' with metathesis ⲩⲉⲕ for ⲗⲉⲕ. Standard Manichaean technical term for the elect (in glossary: ⲉⲕⲗⲉⲕⲧⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲗⲉⲓⲟⲥ).

Hendiadys 'the residue and the remainder' — both ⲥⲱⲭⲡ (Lyc. for ⲥⲱϫⲡ̄ 'remainder') and ⲥⲉⲡⲉ (= ⲥⲉⲡⲉ 'remainder/rest,' in glossary as ⲥⲉⲧⲧⲉ) are synonyms. The doublet emphasizes that the psychic icon is what remains/is left over of the New Man — i.e., the soul-icon distinct from the higher pneumatic Mind-icon.

'The Old Man' in Pauline anthropological register (παλαιὸς ἄνθρωπος, Eph 4:22, Col 3:9) — already in accumulated vocabulary as anthropological pair-partner with ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲃⲣⲣⲉ 'New Man.' Here glosses the somatic-flesh-bound icon.

Verb ⲃⲁϣⲥ̄ recurs in lines 29 and 31 with 3sg.f object — apparently a transitive verb of pouring/spreading the soul. Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲡⲱϣ 'spread, divide' or ⲃⲱⲣϣ̄ 'pour out.' Translated 'pour her' to capture the directional/transferring sense in the soul-descent context.

ⲟⲩⲏⲍ = Lyc. qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱⲍ/ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'add, place upon, contain' (cf. accumulated ϩⲟⲩⲱⲍ 'to add'). With ⲁⲣⲁⲩ 'upon them/over them' = 'which contains/encompasses them all' — the somatic icon as the bodily envelope of the higher two.

ⲧⲣⲟⲫⲏ ⲛ̄ⲧⲃⲓⲟⲩⲱⲙ 'food of eating' — ⲃⲓⲟⲩⲱⲙ likely verbal noun ⲃⲓ-ⲟⲩⲱⲙ 'bringing-eating' or 'consumption.' Manichaean technical context: the soul-icon descends through the act of eating food, by which captive light is mingled into the body.
Lyc. ⲛ̄ϫⲁϫⲉ 'the enemies' (with regular Lyc. ⲝ for ϫ). The psychic icon is poured out unto the enemies — the dark powers/archons that war against the soul.

Translated as 'the Indweller' tentatively. The lexeme is obscure and resists confident parsing. The overlines on ⲕ̄ may indicate a syllabic abbreviation. Possible analyses: (a) ⲡ-ⲉⲧ-ⲕⲏ-ⲛ 'that which is laid up / the deposit'; (b) ⲡ-ⲛⲏⲧⲕ̄-ⲛ 'the firmly-set one' from ⲧⲱⲕ 'stand fast'; (c) some Manichaean technical title not in our glossary. The text identifies ⲡⲛⲧⲕ̄ⲛ with ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲃⲣⲡⲉ 'the New Man' and gives it an icon (line 4). 'Indweller' captures the sense of 'that which exists/dwells in her' (ⲉⲧⲱⲟⲡ ⲛϩⲏⲧⲥ). Flagged for review.
Translated 'blazes a path' / 'sets a way.' Compound: ⲣ̄- ('do/make') + ⲟⲩ- ('a') + ϫⲁⲩ-ⲙⲁⲓⲧ ('way-setting'). Cf. accumulated ⲣⲉϩⲭⲁⲩⲙⲁⲓⲧ 'guide / path-setter' — same root structure.

Translated 'from every life' tentatively. Possibly reduplicated ⲱⲛϩ̄-ⲱⲛϩ̄ 'every-life' or related to ⲍⲱⲱⲛ 'living thing.' The Living Member is redeemed out of all manifestations of life. Awaits parallels.

Translated 'she habitually releases' (lines 13, 14). Likely ϣⲁⲥ-ⲃⲱⲗ habitual + assimilated form, paralleling the cosmologically-significant ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release' (in glossary). Antithetical pair-partner with ⲱⲁⲥⲱⲛϩ̄ 'she habitually lives' (line 19): in the somatic/psychic registers the soul releases what is not hers; in the pneumatic register she lives and joins. Etymology not certain; could alternatively read 'casts off / strips off.'

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲱⲥ ⲉⲙ ⲡⲉ / ⲛⲱⲥ ⲉⲛ ⲛⲉ
notes.decision: Lycopolitan negative construction with ⲉⲙ/ⲉⲛ for Sah. ⲁⲛ. Translates 'is/are not hers' — possessive ⲡⲱⲥ/ⲛⲱⲥ '(thing) of her / (things) of her' + negation.
The terminal letter ⲉ is marked '(?)' by the editor as uncertain. Preserved in coptic field. Likely the start of relative ⲉⲧⲉ continuing into line 16 (ⲉ-ⲧⲉⲥ-... 'which her-...').
Translated 'discord' / 'division.' Likely Lyc. nominal form of ⲡⲱⲣⲭ/ⲡⲱⲣϫ 'separate, divide' (cf. ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary). In the vice-catalogue with ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲟⲥ 'envy.'
Lyc. ⲥⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ = Sah. ⲥⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄ 'join, mingle, blend.' Used here of the soul joining inward with patience and faith — the positive incorporation in the pneumatic register.

Translated 'the hour of life.' This is the alternate name (ϫⲉ ...) of the Virgin of Light who is the robe of the New Man. ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ = Greek ὥρα 'hour, moment' (or = ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ 'hour'); ⲡⲱⲛϩ̄ 'the life.' She is described as both first and last (line 24) — eschatological-soteriological self-identification.
